title: THE COUNT THE MOUNTAIN ASKED FOR
deck: The last count of a four-hundred-year ritual has lost its keeper, and the seismologist wants six thousand people off the island. Illuminara has one night of road to give and no way to read a volcano, so she asks to be taught to count.
shape: Seven scenes across thirty-two hours: a vigil, a dawn that corrects her hands, a council that cannot agree what a hand can know, a test written down before anyone measures, an alarm that finally changes its voice, a night road with a refusal built into it, and a last walk of the wells where the two keepers set their terms.

scenes.title: The Vigil
paragraphs: *The count-house, Port Sinnet · the night before the last count*

Ebben Marrin had been dead since dusk, and the lamp beside his bed was being kept alight the way it had been kept for every Counter of Oru Sinnet for four hundred years: by someone who did not know why.

Illuminara had come to the count-house to ask about a road. She stayed because the door was open and the only person inside was a young woman with her hands flat on her knees, sitting the vigil like an examination.

**Teo**  
You can sit. Nobody speaks of the Mountain in this room.
Teo Marrin had walked the ring of wells behind her great-uncle for nine years. She knew thirty-nine lines of the nightly count by heart, and the fortieth not at all.
Dr Ines Halloran came to the doorway with a roll of paper and did not cross the threshold in her boots.

**Halloran**  
My curve rose for four days and has fallen for thirty hours. After eleven years I know a falling curve means the mountain is letting go, or that it has stopped being able to. The paper does not say which.

**Teo**  
Then why are you here?

**Halloran**  
Because the council will not move on my paper and might move on yours. Say the last line at dawn, whatever it is.

**Teo**  
He kept the fortieth. I have thirty-nine, and I will not give you a number I made up so you can sleep.

**Halloran**  
Then I evacuate on the curve, and the island loses boats again. I am sorry for him. I am not sorry for the question. Four centuries of chanting is a comfort, not a sensor, and I will not ask six thousand people to bet their lives on a lullaby.

Nobody in the room was wrong, and Illuminara felt how little her gifts weighed against that. She could hold the north cliff road open for one night. She could feel the cone loaded in the rock like a bowl on a table, loaded as it had been for centuries, and she could not say what that meant. *I can read how the mountain is held. I cannot read what it intends.*

**Illuminara**  
What is the count for, Teo? Not what it means. What does it do, each night, with your hands?

**Teo**  
It is what we do.

**Illuminara**  
Then teach it to me. Badly, from the beginning, the way you would teach a child. And tell me nothing about what it is for until I have got it wrong.
Teo looked at the lamp for a long time.

**Teo**  
He said an outsider's hand would spoil the water.

**Illuminara**  
Then correct me until it does not.
At the door Halloran hesitated, laid her roll of paper on the step where it would be waiting in the morning, and went away down the hill.

scenes.title: Left Wrist First
paragraphs: *The ring of wells, Oru Sinnet · dawn, the day of the last count*

Seven stone-lipped wells stood in a ring around the mountain's middle slope, each older than the island's records. They began at the Sill Well by the sea gate, where the water was cold as a bell, and Teo set her left wrist into it for nine breaths.

**Teo**  
Left wrist first. You are not reading the water. You are reading how much it differs from the last water.

Illuminara did the Sill as she was shown and found out something she had not expected to learn at her age. She could trace a mountain's load paths through solid rock, and her wrist could not tell cold from cold. A wet nothing. Teo's hand closed over hers and set it down again, slower. *It has been a long time since anyone corrected my hands. I like it more than I should.*
At Cooper's Well Teo said that the water stood. At the Cistern the path forked, and Illuminara went toward the next well because it was shorter.

**Teo**  
Order.

**Illuminara**  
It is thirty paces.

**Teo**  
It is not thirty paces. It is the hand. The hand forgets in ninety seconds, so you go the way it forgot.
At the next well she dried her wrist on her sleeve, and was stopped again.

**Teo**  
Your sleeve is warmer than the water. You have just lied to your own arm.
Illuminara held very still. *The order is not liturgy. It is the reference. Every well is read against the one before it.*

For four hundred years the water at the Elbow had stepped up into the warmest of the seven, which the Counters called the Crown. This dawn it stood. At Dowe's Well on the north terrace, it stepped up. Teo said so to the stones, with no surprise in her voice. Illuminara heard the surprise anyway.
Marit Dowe was waiting at her well with a hen under each arm.

**Marit**  
Six days they have not set foot on the terrace. Anywhere else, yes. Hob says it is the weather.
On the Elbow terrace they counted the birds. The crater-ledge colony lifted at first grey, a hundred birds on an ordinary morning, and Teo tied a knot in her cord for every one. Thirty-one.
Walking down, Illuminara said the three lines under her breath, wells and birds and hens, and heard what the morning had been telling her.

**Illuminara**  
Every line says than. Warmer than the well before. Fewer than yesterday. Hens that will not, as they would not last night. Nothing in the count is a number. It is all a difference from the one before.

**Teo**  
That is what counting is.

**Illuminara**  
Then what is the fortieth line a difference from?
Teo stopped on the path.

**Teo**  
The first night of the Turn. How far the Crown has walked in forty nights. He said you had to be old enough to say it.

**Illuminara**  
It is a subtraction.

**Teo**  
I can see that now. The Crown sat at the Elbow on the first night and sits at Dowe's tonight. One well. In nine years it has never walked. I do not know if one is a great deal, and he took that with him. I will do the sum myself. I will not say it until I know what it weighs.

scenes.title: What a Hand Can Know
paragraphs: *The harbour hall, Port Sinnet · mid-morning*

Councillor Ruan Sethe chaired nine tired people and one memory. Seven years ago he had signed an evacuation order, and the fleet had gone out into a gale that sank three boats and rotted a winter's catch on the quay. The mountain had not coughed.

**Sethe**  
Tell me why today is different, Doctor.

**Halloran**  
I cannot. The curve has fallen, and I do not know whether that is relief or a lid.

**Illuminara**  
What would a falling swarm look like if the heat were still rising?
Halloran began to answer and stopped, as if the answer had a sharp edge.

**Halloran**  
Like a lid. The rock seals, fracturing stops, and the pressure builds with nothing to vent it. But I have no heat. I never had. My needles hear rock break. They cannot feel a well.

**Illuminara**  
Teo's hand can. This dawn the Crown walked from the Elbow to Dowe's Well. The hens refuse the north hollow, and thirty-one birds in a hundred left the ledge. Your curve says calm and the count says warmer. If both are true, it is your lid.

**Halloran**  
Or it is a wrist and a story about hens. A hand is not a thermometer.

**Teo**  
A step is half a degree. Below that we say stands. And your needles cannot tell anyone where.
It landed, because it was true. Halloran's best location for the swarm was a smear five kilometres wide.

**Halloran**  
Blunt both ways, then.

**Sethe**  
I will not move six thousand people on a lullaby or a squiggle.

**Illuminara**  
Then do not. But the count says the Crown is at Dowe's, and nobody here can tell me how long the mountain takes from that to a change in the tremor. Has it happened before?
Teo did not answer at once. She took her great-uncle's cord-book from inside her coat, its knots gone dark with handling, and turned it to two pages she had plainly read before.

**Teo**  
The Turn of 'ninety-eight. The Crown reached Dowe's at the dawn count. And the Turn of two thousand and six, the same.

**Halloran**  
The parish book has 'ninety-eight. The floor hummed at evening bell, and the terrace split before the next first light. And my predecessor's strip chart from two thousand and six is in the cellar. I have never looked at it against a cord.
She sent a boy for the chart. Nobody spoke while he ran. When it came, Halloran laid it on the table beside the cord-book and put her finger on the hum.

**Halloran**  
Eleven hours after the dawn count in 'ninety-eight. Twenty-three in two thousand and six. Two Turns. That is two Turns, and not a law.

**Illuminara**  
Then that is the band we write, and we write that it is two Turns. Let us put down, before anyone measures, what the count says her instruments will find. If we are wrong, you will know by dark and have lost an afternoon.

She wrote on the back of Halloran's own roll, and read it aloud so that nobody could amend it later. Dowe's Well half a degree or more warmer than the Elbow on Halloran's probe, not Teo's wrist. The Sill Well, as a control, within a third of a degree of Halloran's reading from 2019. Carbon dioxide at hen height in the north hollow of at least one percent, where the air should hold four hundredths. And if all three held, the swarm should end its calm as continuous tremor between eleven and twenty-three hours after the dawn count, on the evidence of two Turns. If any of the first three failed, the count was wrong this Turn, and she would say so to the council herself.

**Halloran**  
I will read all seven wells, not three. If your hand and my probe disagree, I want that on the table too.

**Teo**  
The numbers I will give you. The words I keep.

**Sethe**  
And the call is mine. Two instruments agree and the tremor changes. Any household that wants to go early may leave from four o'clock, and any that wants to stay may stay.

scenes.title: Hen Height
paragraphs: *Dowe's Steps, the north terrace · mid-afternoon*
Teo called each well with her wrist before Halloran put the probe in. Halloran wrote down both and said nothing for six wells.

**Halloran**  
Your hand missed a third of a degree at the Cistern.

**Teo**  
It is under a step. It is meant to.

**Halloran**  
So it is blunt too. Good. I was beginning to find your accuracy unbearable.

Dowe's Well came in nine tenths of a degree above the Elbow. The Sill Well sat within a tenth of her reading from seven years back. Then Halloran lowered the gas meter into the hollow behind the terraces, where Marit's hens would not go, and the alarm on it began to chirp like something small and frightened.

**Halloran**  
Four percent. At hen height. It was four hundredths this spring.
She backed up two steps without being told. Marit's hen tucked its head under her arm.

**Halloran**  
In the ash of 'ninety-eight, six sheep died in this hollow before anything fell. I read it in the parish book. I thought it was a footnote.

**Teo**  
It is a line of the count. The hens, that year, and then the sheep.
Halloran looked at the meter, and then at Teo, who stood with her wet left wrist held away from her body so the wind would not warm it.

**Halloran**  
I was afraid of being wrong again. I think I was afraid of the wrong thing.

**Marit**  
Hob will not leave the goats. I will go if they call it. That is how it is in our house.

scenes.title: Harmonic
paragraphs: *The harbour hall, Port Sinnet · evening*
Sethe had the numbers by six o'clock, and he did not move.

**Sethe**  
I said two instruments and a change in the tremor. I have two.

**Halloran**  
I would rather you called it now.

**Sethe**  
I know. And if I move the north slope a day early, then the next time you are right, nobody moves. Teo Marrin. What does the count say?
Teo stood. The hall was quiet in a way the island rarely was.

**Teo**  
The Crown has walked one well, from the Elbow to Dowe's. That is the number. The words stay with the Counters.
At 19:38 the receiver on Halloran's belt changed its voice. For four days it had ticked like a cooling stove. Now it hummed, steadily, as if someone had drawn a bow across the island.

**Halloran**  
Harmonic tremor. Continuous. It began three minutes ago.

**Illuminara**  
Thirteen hours from the dawn count. The band was eleven to twenty-three.

**Halloran**  
Two Turns. I will take it, and I will hate how little it is.
Sethe looked at the paper Illuminara had written that morning, and at the three ticks beside the first three lines, and at the fourth.

**Sethe**  
North slope. Kell and Dowe's Steps, everyone who will walk. The fleet goes out for the dawn run, as planned. The harvest on the south and east comes in. Nobody is carried.

scenes.title: The Throat
paragraphs: *The north cliff road, Oru Sinnet · night*

The only road from Kell and Dowe's Steps to the harbour crossed the Throat, a gully where cut rock hung beneath sixty metres of loose scree. Illuminara took its weight with the window shut: a held load, not a deep contact. She found its carrier first, slabs wedged on a lip each resting on the next, then its extent, forty metres of slope above the road, and then she said aloud how long she could keep it.

**Illuminara**  
Lamps in pairs. Nothing runs. Halloran reads me the tremor every ten minutes so I know when it leans.
They came down for three hours in the dark, a thousand lamps at a walking pace. A child asked her whether the mountain was angry, and she said she did not think anyone had asked it yet.
Marit came last, with the hens in baskets.

**Marit**  
I came down with the first lamps and went back up for these. Hob is on the ridge with eight other households and will not come.

**Illuminara**  
Then we will not carry him. We will ask him what he needs.

The ridge above Dowe's Steps stood higher than the hollow. Hob Dowe sat on a stone with his arms crossed, and his twelve goats stood penned on the slope at his back behind three hurdles. Teo and Illuminara laid it out where he could refuse it: stay above the hens' line, a meter lent by Halloran, a radio, one of Marit's hens in a basket on the path. When the hen sat down, or the alarm began, they would climb to the saddle.

**Hob**  
Seven years ago this council took my goats down to a quay and the quay had no grass. Eleven winters I have kept these twelve. They are the only thing in this house that is not owed to somebody.

**Teo**  
The gas runs low. It will find the pen before it finds you.

**Hob**  
It found the sheep on the low ridge in 'ninety-eight. Not the high one. I read the same parish book you did.
He looked at the meter, not at her.

**Hob**  
Your hen sits at the foot of the hollow. A goat is lower than a hen.
Illuminara saw that he was right, and that nobody had said it.

**Illuminara**  
Then the meter does not belong beside your boot.

**Hob**  
It hangs from the post above the pen, at a kid's head. If it sings there, it has already reached them, and I have one breath to be on the path. I take the gate-bar down now, not then. They can climb if they have a mind to. I will not drive them. I will not stand there counting, either.

**Marit**  
And when the hen sits?

**Hob**  
Then I go, and the ones that will not follow do not. Say it so I have heard myself say it.

He lifted the gate-bar off its pegs and laid it in the grass, then took the meter and hung it on the post himself, above the pen, where he had said. Nobody ordered him, and nobody was left without a way to hear.

scenes.title: The Fortieth Line
paragraphs: *The Elbow Well, Oru Sinnet · dawn*

At 03:34 the meter on the post began to sound. The gate-bar had been down since dusk, and the goats had had the whole night to climb if they had a mind to; Hob did not stop to drive them. Forty-one people went up to the saddle in the dark, Hob last among them, and he did not turn round. At 03:52 the north terrace split along the old scar of 'ninety-eight and breathed out steam, ash and a stream of gas that ran down the hollows like water. Dowe's Steps was empty. The terraces were buried. The hollow where the hens would not go was full of air that could not be breathed.

Nobody died. Of Hob's twelve goats, five had climbed through the open gate and seven had not, and Hob counted them in the grey. It was Marit, up from the quay, who walked to him and stood a long while without saying anything.
At first light forty-one boats went out for the dawn run on the south side, lamps still lit, because the fish did not know about the mountain.
The Counters walk at dawn, even after a night like that one. Teo took the left wrist to the Sill Well, and Illuminara and Halloran followed her in order, a pace apart.

**Teo**  
Sill steps up from the sea. Cooper's stands. The Cistern steps up. The Elbow cools. The Crown has walked, and it is at Dowe's, and it is still walking.
She said the birds, and the hens, and then the thing that had waited in the room since Ebben died.

**Teo**  
Forty nights. One well. The old word for this line is asked. I thought it meant the Mountain asks us to leave. I think it only means she has asked a question, and the count is how the island answers.
Nobody spoke of Ebben. The lamp in the count-house had been put out at dawn by the person who kept it.
At the Cistern, where the path forks, Teo stopped and did not take the shorter way.

**Teo**  
You will say I cannot do this alone. I could not today. I had thirty-nine lines and she had a chart in a cellar. Here is what I will give. The probe goes in the log, never in the count. When hand and probe disagree, both are written down and neither is corrected to match. You read the wells in order, beside a Counter, and you hold the wrist at the Sill as well as the needle.

**Halloran**  
And you hear my needles before the council does. If they speak first, you hear it that hour, not that evening.

**Teo**  
Yes. And either of us may stop it, and say why.

**Halloran**  
What does it cost you?

**Teo**  
The ring. Four hundred years, and I am the one who opens it. He would have said an outsider's hand spoils the water. I think he was afraid of being the last. I would rather be the first who was taught.

Sethe would put his name under it that week, to say that two keepers had chosen it and no more. It was theirs to write, and Teo wrote it first on the back of the roll of paper that had been waiting on the step.
At the Elbow, Halloran put her left wrist into the water, and Teo watched her for nine breaths before she spoke.

**Teo**  
Slower.

**Halloran**  
It is cold.

**Teo**  
It is cold. Now tell me the difference.
Illuminara stood at the lip of the well with her own wrist in the water, a beginner again, and the sun came up on three people counting what the mountain had told them.

critic_line: Illuminara first learns what the island's count can and cannot mean, then makes herself teachable to the people who must live with the alarm: Hob corrects her instrument and freely chooses the threshold he will obey, while Teo and Halloran replace rival custody with reciprocal, terminable stewardship; the resulting warning saves forty-one people and the working island without pretending the lost terraces and seven goats did not matter.

shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-heavy collaboration between ritual and instrument, with a satisfying pre-registered prediction and a well-earned closing exchange. Strong idea (counting as difference). Held back by dense proper nouns, a slightly procedural middle, and a mostly resolved, low-tension arc.

A gripping, unusually humane synthesis of ritual knowledge and scientific testing, carried by sharp dialogue, escalating stakes, and morally serious choices. The distinctive counting system, earned cooperation, and bittersweet handling of Hob’s goats should remain vivid, while the satisfying ending makes recommendation especially likely.
shared_reservations: Dowe's Well half a degree or more warmer than the Elbow on Halloran's probe, not Teo's wrist. The Sill Well, as a control, within a third of a degree of Halloran's reading from 2019.

translation_sl.title: ŠTETJE, ZA KATERO JE PROSILA GORA
translation_sl.deck: Zadnje štetje štiristoletnega obreda je izgubilo svojega varuha, seizmologinja pa želi z otoka umakniti šest tisoč ljudi. Illuminara lahko za eno noč obdrži cesto odprto, vendar ne zna brati vulkana, zato prosi, naj jo naučijo šteti.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v dvaintridesetih urah: bdenje, zora, ki popravi njene roke, svet, ki se ne more zediniti, kaj lahko ve roka, preizkus, zapisan, preden kdo kaj izmeri, alarm, ki končno spremeni glas, nočna cesta z vanjo vgrajeno zavrnitvijo ter zadnji obhod vodnjakov, pri katerem varuha določita svoje pogoje.

scenes.title: Bdenje
paragraphs: *Hiša štetja, Port Sinnet · noč pred zadnjim štetjem*
Ebben Marrin je bil mrtev od mraka, svetilka ob njegovi postelji pa je gorela tako, kakor je gorela za vsakega Števca Oru Sinneta štiristo let: prižgana po zaslugi nekoga, ki ni vedel zakaj.

Illuminara je prišla v hišo štetja vprašat za cesto. Ostala je, ker so bila vrata odprta in je bila edina oseba v notranjosti mlada ženska z dlanmi plosko na kolenih, ki je sedela pri bdenju kakor na izpitu.

**Teo**  
Lahko sedeš. V tej sobi nihče ne govori o Gori.
Teo Marrin je devet let hodila po krogu vodnjakov za svojim prastricem. Devetintrideset vrstic nočnega štetja je znala na pamet, štiridesete pa sploh ne.
Dr. Ines Halloran je prišla do vrat z zvitkom papirja in v škornjih ni prestopila praga.

**Halloran**  
Moja krivulja je štiri dni naraščala in trideset ur padala. Po enajstih letih vem, da padajoča krivulja pomeni, da gora popušča ali da tega ne zmore več. Papir ne pove, kaj od tega.

**Teo**  
Zakaj si potem tukaj?

**Halloran**  
Ker se svet zaradi mojega papirja ne bo premaknil, zaradi tvojega pa bi se lahko. Ob zori izgovori zadnjo vrstico, kakršna koli že je.

**Teo**  
Štirideseto je zadržal zase. Jaz jih imam devetintrideset in ne bom ti dala številke, ki sem si jo izmislila, da boš lahko spala.

**Halloran**  
Potem evakuiram zaradi krivulje in otok spet izgubi čolne. Žal mi je zanj. Za vprašanje pa mi ni žal. Štiri stoletja petja so tolažba, ne tipalo, in šest tisoč ljudi ne bom prosila, naj svoje življenje stavijo na uspavanko.

Nihče v sobi se ni motil in Illuminara je začutila, kako malo tehtajo njeni darovi ob tem. Cesto ob severni pečini je lahko za eno noč obdržala odprto. Čutila je stožec, napet v skali kakor skleda na mizi, napet tako, kakor je bil stoletja, in ni mogla reči, kaj to pomeni. *Lahko preberem, kako je gora podprta. Ne morem prebrati, kaj namerava.*

**Illuminara**  
Čemu je štetje namenjeno, Teo? Ne kaj pomeni. Kaj vsako noč naredi s tvojimi rokami?

**Teo**  
To je tisto, kar počnemo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem me ga nauči. Slabo, od začetka, kakor bi učila otroka. In nič mi ne povej, čemu je namenjeno, dokler se ne zmotim.
Teo je dolgo gledala svetilko.

**Teo**  
Rekel je, da bi roka tujca pokvarila vodo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem me popravljaj, dokler je ne bo.
Halloran je pri vratih oklevala, položila zvitek papirja na stopnico, kjer jo bo čakal zjutraj, in odšla po hribu navzdol.

scenes.title: Najprej levo zapestje
paragraphs: *Krog vodnjakov, Oru Sinnet · zora na dan zadnjega štetja*

Sedem vodnjakov s kamnitimi robovi je stalo v krogu okoli srednjega pobočja gore, vsak starejši od otoških zapisov. Začeli so pri vodnjaku Prag ob morskih vratih, kjer je bila voda mrzla kakor zvon, Teo pa je vanjo za devet vdihov potopila levo zapestje.

**Teo**  
Najprej levo zapestje. Ne bereš vode. Bereš, koliko se razlikuje od prejšnje vode.

Illuminara je pri Pragu naredila, kakor so ji pokazali, in izvedela nekaj, česar se pri svojih letih ni pričakovala naučiti. Skozi trdno skalo je lahko sledila potem obremenitve gore, njeno zapestje pa ni ločilo mraza od mraza. Mokri nič. Teina roka se je sklenila okoli njene in jo znova položila v vodo, počasneje. *Že dolgo mi nihče ni popravljal rok. Všeč mi je bolj, kot bi mi smelo biti.*
Pri Cooperjevem vodnjaku je Teo rekla, da voda stoji. Pri Cisterni se je pot razcepila in Illuminara je krenila proti naslednjemu vodnjaku, ker je bilo krajše.

**Teo**  
Vrstni red.

**Illuminara**  
Trideset korakov je.

**Teo**  
Ni trideset korakov. Roka je. Roka pozabi v devetdesetih sekundah, zato greš po poti, po kateri je pozabila.
Pri naslednjem vodnjaku si je obrisala zapestje v rokav in bila znova ustavljena.

**Teo**  
Tvoj rokav je toplejši od vode. Pravkar si lagala lastni roki.
Illuminara je obstala povsem pri miru. *Vrstni red ni obredje. Je referenca. Vsak vodnjak berejo glede na prejšnjega.*

Štiristo let je voda pri Komolcu stopila navzgor do najtoplejšega od sedmih, ki so ga Števci imenovali Krona. To zoro je stala. Pri Dowejevem vodnjaku na severni terasi je stopila navzgor. Teo je to povedala kamnom brez presenečenja v glasu. Illuminara ga je kljub temu slišala.
Marit Dowe je čakala pri svojem vodnjaku s kokošjo pod vsako roko.

**Marit**  
Šest dni niso stopile na teraso. Kamor koli drugam, da. Hob pravi, da je vreme.
Na terasi pri Komolcu so prešteli ptice. Kolonija na robu kraterja je poletela ob prvi sivini, sto ptic navadnega jutra, Teo pa je za vsako zavezala vozel v vrvico. Enaintrideset.
Na poti navzdol je Illuminara potiho ponovila tri vrstice, vodnjake, ptice in kokoši, ter slišala, kaj ji je pripovedovalo jutro.

**Illuminara**  
Vsaka vrstica pravi kot. Toplejši kot prejšnji vodnjak. Manj kot včeraj. Kokoši, ki nočejo, kakor niso hotele sinoči. Nič v štetju ni številka. Vse je razlika od prejšnjega.

**Teo**  
To je štetje.

**Illuminara**  
Od česa se potem razlikuje štirideseta vrstica?
Teo se je ustavila na poti.

**Teo**  
Od prve noči Obrata. Kako daleč je Krona prehodila v štiridesetih nočeh. Rekel je, da moraš biti dovolj star, da jo izgovoriš.

**Illuminara**  
Odštevanje je.

**Teo**  
Zdaj to vidim. Krona je prvo noč sedela pri Komolcu, nocoj pa sedi pri Dowejevem. En vodnjak. V devetih letih ni nikoli hodila. Ne vem, ali je ena veliko, on pa je to odnesel s seboj. Račun bom naredila sama. Ne bom ga izgovorila, dokler ne bom vedela, koliko tehta.

scenes.title: Kaj lahko ve roka
paragraphs: *Pristaniška dvorana, Port Sinnet · dopoldne*

Svetnik Ruan Sethe je predsedoval devetim utrujenim ljudem in enemu spominu. Pred sedmimi leti je podpisal ukaz za evakuacijo, flota pa je odplula v vihar, ki je potopil tri čolne in pustil zimski ulov gniti na pomolu. Gora ni zakašljala.

**Sethe**  
Povejte mi, zakaj je danes drugače, doktorica.

**Halloran**  
Ne morem. Krivulja je padla in ne vem, ali je to olajšanje ali pokrov.

**Illuminara**  
Kako bi bil videti pojemajoč roj, če bi toplota še vedno naraščala?
Halloran je začela odgovarjati in se ustavila, kakor da ima odgovor oster rob.

**Halloran**  
Kakor pokrov. Skala se zatesni, lomljenje se ustavi, pritisk pa narašča, ne da bi se imel kam sprostiti. Toda toplote nimam. Nikoli je nisem imela. Moje igle slišijo lomljenje skale. Vodnjaka ne morejo čutiti.

**Illuminara**  
Teina roka ga lahko. To zoro se je Krona premaknila od Komolca do Dowejevega vodnjaka. Kokoši se izogibajo severni kotanji in od sto ptic jih je z roba vzletelo enaintrideset. Vaša krivulja pravi mir, štetje pa topleje. Če drži oboje, je to vaš pokrov.

**Halloran**  
Ali pa sta zapestje in zgodba o kokoših. Roka ni termometer.

**Teo**  
Korak je pol stopinje. Pod tem rečemo, da stoji. Vaše igle pa nikomur ne morejo povedati, kje.
Zadelo je, ker je bilo res. Halloran je lahko roj najbolje umestila le v pet kilometrov širok madež.

**Halloran**  
Torej topo v obe smeri.

**Sethe**  
Šest tisoč ljudi ne bom premaknil zaradi uspavanke ali čačke.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jih ne. Toda štetje pravi, da je Krona pri Dowejevem, nihče tukaj pa mi ne zna povedati, koliko časa gora potrebuje od tega do spremembe tresenja. Se je to že zgodilo?
Teo ni odgovorila takoj. Iz notranjosti plašča je vzela vrvno knjigo svojega prastrica, katere vozli so od prijemanja potemneli, in jo odprla na dveh straneh, ki ju je očitno že brala.

**Teo**  
Obrat leta osemindevetdeset. Krona je pri jutranjem štetju dosegla Dowejev vodnjak. In enako ob Obratu leta dva tisoč šest.

**Halloran**  
Župnijska knjiga ima osemindevetdeseto. Tla so zabrnela ob večernem zvonu, terasa pa se je razklala pred naslednjo prvo svetlobo. Trak mojega predhodnika iz leta dva tisoč šest je v kleti. Nikoli ga nisem primerjala z vrvico.
Po trak je poslala dečka. Med njegovim tekom nihče ni spregovoril. Ko ga je prinesel, ga je Halloran položila na mizo ob vrvno knjigo in položila prst na brnenje.

**Halloran**  
Enajst ur po jutranjem štetju leta osemindevetdeset. Triindvajset leta dva tisoč šest. Dva Obrata. To sta dva Obrata, ne zakon.

**Illuminara**  
Potem zapišemo ta razpon in zapišemo, da gre za dva Obrata. Preden kdo kaj izmeri, zapišimo, kaj naj bi po štetju našli njeni instrumenti. Če se motimo, boste vedeli do mraka in izgubili eno popoldne.

Pisala je na hrbtno stran Halloraninega zvitka in besede prebrala na glas, da jih pozneje ne bi mogel nihče spremeniti. Dowejev vodnjak bo na Halloranini sondi, ne na Teinem zapestju, za pol stopinje ali več toplejši od Komolca. Vodnjak Prag, ki bo kontrola, bo od Halloranine meritve iz leta 2019 odstopal za manj kot tretjino stopinje. Ogljikovega dioksida bo na višini kokoši v severni kotanji vsaj en odstotek, kjer bi ga moral zrak vsebovati štiri stotinke. In če bodo držale vse tri ugotovitve, naj bi roj med enajsto in triindvajseto uro po jutranjem štetju prekinil svoj mir in prešel v neprekinjeni tremor, sodeč po dveh Obratih. Če katera od prvih treh ne bi držala, bi bilo štetje ob tem Obratu napačno in sama bi to povedala svetu.

**Halloran**  
Prebrala bom vseh sedem vodnjakov, ne treh. Če se tvoja roka in moja sonda ne strinjata, hočem tudi to na mizi.

**Teo**  
Številke vam bom dala. Besede obdržim.

**Sethe**  
Odločitev pa je moja. Dva instrumenta se strinjata in tresenje se spremeni. Vsako gospodinjstvo, ki želi oditi prej, lahko odide od štirih naprej, in vsako, ki želi ostati, lahko ostane.

scenes.title: Na višini kokoši
paragraphs: *Dowejeve stopnice, severna terasa · sredi popoldneva*
Teo je z zapestjem določila vsak vodnjak, preden je Halloran vanj spustila sondo. Halloran je zapisala oboje in šest vodnjakov ni rekla ničesar.

**Halloran**  
Pri Cisterni se je tvoja roka zmotila za tretjino stopinje.

**Teo**  
Manj kot en korak je. Tako je mišljeno.

**Halloran**  
Torej je tudi to topo. Dobro. Tvoja natančnost mi je že postajala neznosna.

Dowejev vodnjak je bil za devet desetin stopinje toplejši od Komolca. Vodnjak Prag je bil od njene meritve izpred sedmih let oddaljen za desetinko. Nato je Halloran spustila merilnik plina v kotanjo za terasami, kamor Maritine kokoši niso hotele, alarm na njem pa je začel čivkati kakor nekaj majhnega in prestrašenega.

**Halloran**  
Štirje odstotki. Na višini kokoši. To pomlad so bile štiri stotinke.
Brez opozorila je stopila dve stopnici nazaj. Maritina kokoš je skrila glavo pod njeno roko.

**Halloran**  
V pepelu leta osemindevetdeset je v tej kotanji poginilo šest ovc, preden je kar koli padlo. Prebrala sem v župnijski knjigi. Mislila sem, da je opomba pod črto.

**Teo**  
Vrstica štetja je. Tistega leta kokoši, nato ovce.
Halloran je pogledala merilnik in nato Teo, ki je stala z mokrim levim zapestjem odmaknjenim od telesa, da ga veter ne bi segrel.

**Halloran**  
Bala sem se, da bi se spet zmotila. Mislim, da sem se bala napačne stvari.

**Marit**  
Hob ne bo zapustil koz. Jaz bom odšla, če razglasijo. Tako je pri naši hiši.

scenes.title: Harmonični tremor
paragraphs: *Pristaniška dvorana, Port Sinnet · večer*
Sethe je številke dobil do šestih in se ni premaknil.

**Sethe**  
Rekel sem dva instrumenta in sprememba tresenja. Imam dva.

**Halloran**  
Raje bi, da razglasite zdaj.

**Sethe**  
Vem. Če pa severno pobočje premaknem dan prezgodaj, se naslednjič, ko boste imeli prav, ne bo premaknil nihče. Teo Marrin. Kaj pravi štetje?
Teo je vstala. Dvorana je bila tiha tako, kakor je bil otok redko.

**Teo**  
Krona je prehodila en vodnjak, od Komolca do Dowejevega. To je številka. Besede ostanejo pri Števcih.
Ob 19:38 je sprejemnik na Halloraninem pasu spremenil glas. Štiri dni je tiktakal kakor peč, ki se ohlaja. Zdaj je enakomerno brnel, kakor da bi nekdo z lokom potegnil čez otok.

**Halloran**  
Harmonični tremor. Neprekinjen. Začel se je pred tremi minutami.

**Illuminara**  
Trinajst ur od jutranjega štetja. Razpon je bil od enajst do triindvajset.

**Halloran**  
Dva Obrata. Sprejela bom in sovražila, kako malo je to.
Sethe je pogledal papir, ki ga je Illuminara napisala tisto jutro, tri kljukice ob prvih treh vrsticah in četrto vrstico.

**Sethe**  
Severno pobočje. Kell in Dowejeve stopnice, vsi, ki bodo hodili. Flota gre po načrtu na jutranjo plovbo. Žetev na jugu in vzhodu se spravi. Nikogar ne nosijo.

scenes.title: Grlo
paragraphs: *Cesta ob severni pečini, Oru Sinnet · noč*

Edina cesta od Kella in Dowejevih stopnic do pristanišča je prečkala Grlo, jarek, v katerem je izsekana skala visela pod šestdesetimi metri sipkega grušča. Illuminara je njegovo težo prevzela z zaprtim oknom: držana obremenitev, ne globok stik. Najprej je našla njen nosilec, plošče, zagozdene na robu, kjer je vsaka slonela na naslednji, nato njen obseg, štirideset metrov pobočja nad cesto, in potem na glas povedala, kako dolgo jo lahko drži.

**Illuminara**  
Svetilke v parih. Nihče ne teče. Halloran mi vsakih deset minut prebere tremor, da vem, kdaj se nagne.
Tri ure so se v temi spuščali navzdol, tisoč svetilk s hitrostjo hoje. Otrok jo je vprašal, ali je gora jezna, in rekla je, da po njenem tega še nihče ni vprašal.
Marit je prišla zadnja s kokošmi v košarah.

**Marit**  
Prišla sem dol s prvimi svetilkami in se vrnila ponje. Hob je na grebenu z osmimi drugimi gospodinjstvi in noče priti.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ga ne bomo nosili. Vprašali ga bomo, kaj potrebuje.

Greben nad Dowejevimi stopnicami je stal višje od kotanje. Hob Dowe je sedel na kamnu s prekrižanimi rokami, njegovih dvanajst koz pa je stalo zaprtih na pobočju za njegovim hrbtom, za tremi ogradami. Teo in Illuminara sta mu načrt razložili tam, kjer ga je lahko zavrnil: ostati nad črto kokoši, merilnik, ki ga posodi Halloran, radio, ena Maritina kokoš v košari na poti. Ko bi kokoš sedla ali bi se oglasil alarm, bi se povzpeli na sedlo.

**Hob**  
Pred sedmimi leti je ta svet odpeljal moje koze na pomol, na pomolu pa ni bilo trave. Enajst zim skrbim za teh dvanajst. So edino v tej hiši, kar ni dolgovano nekomu.

**Teo**  
Plin teče nizko. Ogrado bo našel, preden bo našel tebe.

**Hob**  
Leta osemindevetdeset je našel ovce na nizkem grebenu. Ne na visokem. Prebral sem isto župnijsko knjigo kot ti.
Pogledal je merilnik, ne nje.

**Hob**  
Tvoja kokoš sedi ob vznožju kotanje. Koza je nižja od kokoši.
Illuminara je videla, da ima prav in da tega ni rekel nihče.

**Illuminara**  
Potem merilnik ne sodi ob tvoj čevelj.

**Hob**  
Visi s stebra nad ogrado, v višini kozličkove glave. Če zapoje tam, jih je že dosegel, jaz pa imam en vdih časa, da stopim na pot. Zapah snamem zdaj, ne takrat. Lahko se povzpnejo, če se jim zahoče. Ne bom jih priganjal. Tudi stal ne bom tam in štel.

**Marit**  
In ko kokoš sede?

**Hob**  
Takrat grem, tiste, ki ne bodo sledile, pa ne. Povej, da bom slišal samega sebe to izreči.
Dvignil je zapah s klinov in ga položil v travo, nato vzel merilnik in ga sam obesil na steber nad ogrado, tja, kamor je rekel. Nihče mu ni ukazal in nihče ni ostal brez načina, da bi slišal.

scenes.title: Štirideseta vrstica
paragraphs: *Vodnjak Komolec, Oru Sinnet · zora*

Ob 03:34 se je oglasil merilnik na stebru. Zapah je bil od mraka spuščen, koze pa so imele vso noč, da bi se povzpele, če bi se jim zahotelo; Hob se ni ustavljal, da bi jih priganjal. Enainštirideset ljudi se je v temi povzpelo na sedlo, Hob zadnji med njimi, in ni se ozrl. Ob 03:52 se je severna terasa razklala vzdolž stare brazgotine iz leta osemindevetdeset ter izdihnila paro, pepel in tok plina, ki je stekel po kotanjah kakor voda. Dowejeve stopnice so bile prazne. Terase so bile zasute. Kotanja, kamor kokoši niso hotele, je bila polna zraka, ki ga ni bilo mogoče dihati.

Nihče ni umrl. Od Hobovih dvanajstih koz jih je pet šlo skozi odprta vrata navzgor, sedem pa ne, Hob pa jih je štel v sivini. Marit, ki je prišla s pomola, je stopila k njemu in dolgo stala, ne da bi kar koli rekla.
Ob prvi svetlobi je enainštirideset čolnov odplulo na jutranjo plovbo po južni strani, svetilke so še gorele, ker ribe niso vedele za goro.
Števci hodijo ob zori, tudi po takšni noči. Teo je levo zapestje odnesla k vodnjaku Prag, Illuminara in Halloran pa sta ji v pravilnem vrstnem redu sledili korak narazen.

**Teo**  
Prag stopi navzgor od morja. Cooperjev stoji. Cisterna stopi navzgor. Komolec se hladi. Krona je hodila in je pri Dowejevem, pa še hodi.
Izgovorila je ptice in kokoši ter nato tisto, kar je čakalo v sobi, odkar je umrl Ebben.

**Teo**  
Štirideset noči. En vodnjak. Stara beseda za to vrstico je vprašano. Mislila sem, da pomeni, da nas Gora prosi, naj odidemo. Mislim, da pomeni le, da je zastavila vprašanje, štetje pa je način, kako otok odgovori.
Nihče ni govoril o Ebbnu. Svetilko v hiši štetja je ob zori ugasnila oseba, ki jo je ohranjala prižgano.
Pri Cisterni, kjer se pot razcepi, se je Teo ustavila in ni izbrala krajše poti.

**Teo**  
Rekla boš, da tega ne morem početi sama. Danes nisem mogla. Imela sem devetintrideset vrstic, ona pa graf v kleti. To bom dala: sonda gre v dnevnik, nikoli v štetje. Kadar se roka in sonda ne strinjata, se zapiše oboje in nič se ne popravi, da bi se ujemalo. Vodnjake bereš v vrstnem redu ob Števcu in pri Pragu v vodo držiš tudi zapestje, ne le igle.

**Halloran**  
Ti pa slišiš moje igle pred svetom. Če spregovorijo prve, jih slišiš tisto uro, ne tisti večer.

**Teo**  
Da. In katera koli od naju lahko to ustavi in pove zakaj.

**Halloran**  
Kaj te to stane?

**Teo**  
Krog. Štiristo let in jaz sem tista, ki ga odpira. Rekel bi, da roka tujca pokvari vodo. Mislim, da se je bal biti zadnji. Raje bi bila prva, ki so jo naučili.

Sethe se je tisti teden podpisal pod to, da je potrdil le, da sta se tako odločila dva varuha, in nič več. Zapisati sta morala sama, Teo pa je prva pisala na hrbtno stran zvitka papirja, ki je čakal na stopnici.
Pri Komolcu je Halloran potopila levo zapestje v vodo, Teo pa jo je devet vdihov opazovala, preden je spregovorila.

**Teo**  
Počasneje.

**Halloran**  
Mrzla je.

**Teo**  
Mrzla je. Zdaj mi povej razliko.
Illuminara je stala na robu vodnjaka z lastnim zapestjem v vodi, znova začetnica, sonce pa je vzšlo nad tremi ljudmi, ki so šteli, kaj jim je povedala gora.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara se najprej nauči, kaj otoško štetje lahko pomeni in česa ne, nato pa se prepusti učenju ljudi, ki morajo živeti z alarmom: Hob popravi njen instrument in svobodno izbere prag, ki ga bo upošteval, Teo in Halloran pa tekmujoče varovanje nadomestita z vzajemnim skrbništvom, ki ga je mogoče končati; nastalo opozorilo reši enainštirideset ljudi in delujoči otok, ne da bi se pretvarjalo, da izgubljene terase in sedem koz niso pomembni.
